documents.title: Inland Coastal Fisheries
documents.content:
# SECTOR PROFILE: FISHERIES (DoF & BFRI Protocols)
## Context: Bangladesh is the 3rd largest inland fish producer globally.

### 1. Inland Open Water (Haors & Beels - e.g., Sunamganj, Mymensingh, Netrokona, Natore)
- **Primary Hazard:** Flash Floods (Pre-monsoon), River Erosion.
- **Vulnerability:** Sudden water level rises wash away fish from open waters; destroys cage culture infrastructure.
- **Pre-Event Action (48h):** Harvest mature fish (Rui, Katla, Ilish, Pangasius) immediately. Secure floating cage nets with heavy anchors.
- **Post-Event Recovery:** Restock with fast-growing fingerlings (Tilapia, Silver Carp) provided by Department of Fisheries (DoF). Apply lime (CaCO3 at 250 kg/ha) to stabilize water pH and clear turbidity after floodwater recedes.

### 2. Coastal Aquaculture (Shrimp Gher/Mouth - e.g., Satkhira, Khulna, Bagerhat, Cox's Bazar)
- **Primary Hazard:** Tropical Cyclone, Tidal Surge, Salinity Intrusion.
- **Vulnerability:** Embankment breaches flush out shrimp/fish; extreme salinity spikes cause mass mortality in freshwater prawns (Golda).
- **Pre-Event Action (48h):** Lower pond water levels by 20% to prevent wave overtopping. Reinforce earthen embankments with bamboo nets and sandbags. Close polder sluice gates.
- **Post-Event Recovery:** Repair breached sluice gates immediately. Flush ponds with freshwater if available. Apply agricultural gypsum (2 t/ha) to pond soils to bind excess sodium (Na+).

documents.title: Cyclone Storm
documents.content:
# Hazard Protocol: Tropical Cyclone & Severe Local Storm
## Context: Coastal & Haor Regions (Satkhira, Khulna, Barisal, Sylhet)
### Immediate Actions (0-48 Hours)
- **Embankments**: Sandbag vulnerable points on polders. Close all sluice gates (Sluice Board protocols) to prevent tidal surge intrusion.
- **Propping**: Bamboo propping for tall crops (Banana, Sugarcane, late Aman rice).
- **Harvest**: Harvest mature crops (Potato, Vegetables, mature Aman) immediately.
- **Shelters**: Evacuate livestock and humans to designated Cyclone Shelters (CCB).

### Protective Measures (1-2 Weeks)
- **Saltwater Flushing**: If tidal surge breaches embankments, immediately pump or channel freshwater to flush salt from soil profiles before it penetrates deeper.
- **Debris Clearing**: Remove salt-contaminated debris from agricultural lands to prevent secondary salinization.

### Contingency & Recovery
- **Salinity Spike**: Apply agricultural gypsum (2-3 tons/ha) to displace sodium ions if soil EC > 4 dS/m.
- **Replanting**: Use salt-tolerant varieties (BR-11, BRRI Dhan53, BRRI Dhan54) or switch to sunflower/maize in severely affected coastal belts.

documents.title: Drought Heat Wave
documents.content:
# Hazard Protocol: Drought & Heat Wave
## Context: Barind Tract (Rajshahi, Rangpur) & Pre-Monsoon (Aus Season)
### Immediate Actions (0-48 Hours)
- **AWD Technique**: Implement Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) in Boro rice. Use a simple PVC pipe (Tensiometer) to irrigate only when water level drops 15cm below soil surface. Saves 30% water.
- **Mulching**: Apply straw mulch (5-7 cm) around potato and vegetable bases to reduce soil evaporation.
- **Water Scheduling**: Irrigate during early morning (6 AM) or late evening (5 PM) to minimize evaporative loss.

### Protective Measures (1-2 Weeks)
- **Heat Stress Mitigation**: Spray water on vegetable canopies (cucurbitaceae, solanaceae) during peak heat (12 PM - 3 PM).
- **Nutrient Adjustment**: Reduce nitrogenous fertilizers (which promote lush, water-demanding growth); increase Potash (MOP) to improve plant cell turgor and drought resistance.

### Contingency & Recovery
- **Crop Failure**: If Boro rice fails at panicle initiation, plow and plant short-duration pulses (Masoor, Chickpea) or Maize if residual moisture permits.

documents.title: Flood Flash Flood
documents.content:
# Hazard Protocol: Flood & Flash Flood
## Context: Bangladesh Deltaic Agriculture
### Immediate Actions (0-48 Hours)
- **Drainage**: Clear blocked drainage channels and culverts using community labor (Kazal/Shramik).
- **Harvest**: If Aman rice is at dough/mature stage and flash flood is imminent, harvest immediately even if moisture content is high (use tarpaulins for drying).
- **Livestock**: Move cattle and poultry to elevated cyclone shelters or raised platforms (Machrang).
- **Seed Storage**: Move stored seeds (BRRI varieties) and fertilizers to waterproof, elevated rooms.

### Protective Measures (1-2 Weeks)
- **Post-Flood Drainage**: Dig peripheral trenches (1.5 ft deep) around fields to drain stagnant water within 3-5 days to prevent root rot.
- **Disease Management**: Spray fungicides (e.g., Tilt 250 EC @ 1ml/L) if bacterial leaf blight or sheath blight symptoms appear post-recession.
- **Nutrient Recovery**: Apply urea top-dressing (20-30 kg/ha) once water recedes to stimulate tillering recovery.

### Contingency & Recovery
- **Crop Loss >70%**: Transition to short-duration crops (e.g., BRRI Dhan56, Moong bean, or quick-growing vegetables like Spinach/Lalshak) using residual soil moisture.
- **Fisheries**: Restock flooded beels/haors with carp fingerlings once water quality stabilizes.

documents.title: Cattle Poultry Protocols
documents.content:
# SECTOR PROFILE: LIVESTOCK & POULTRY (DLS & BLRI Protocols)

### 1. Cattle & Goat (e.g., Sirajganj, Kurigram, Jamalpur, Pabna)
- **Primary Hazard:** Riverine Flood, Flash Flood.
- **Vulnerability:** Drowning, loss of shelter, severe post-flood fodder crisis, waterborne diseases (bloat, foot rot).
- **Pre-Event Action (48h):** Evacuate cattle to elevated cyclone/flood shelters (Machrang / Killa) or high-ground community pastures. Stockpile dry fodder (hay, straw, urea-molasses treated straw) for 15 days.
- **Post-Event Recovery:** Provide emergency fodder blocks and mineral licks. Treat for foot rot with 5% copper sulphate foot baths. Ensure access to clean, arsenic/contamination-free tube-well water.

### 2. Poultry (Broiler & Layer - Nationwide, highly sensitive to Heatwaves & Floods)
- **Primary Hazard:** Heat Wave, Cold Wave, Flood (shed destruction).
- **Vulnerability:** Broilers suffer massive mortality at >35°C. Floods destroy low-lying sheds and contaminate feed with mycotoxins.
- **Pre-Event Action (Heatwave):** Provide electrolytes (Vitamin C, Potassium Chloride) in drinking water. Install foggers/sprinklers on shed roofs. Reduce stocking density by 20%.
- **Pre-Event Action (Flood):** Relocate birds to elevated shelters. Store feed on plastic pallets above flood level in airtight drums.

documents.title: Bd Agro Calendar
documents.content:
# Bangladesh Agro-Ecological Seasonal Calendar
## Crucial for aligning HazardNet Lead-Time with Crop Stages

### 1. Kharif-I (Pre-Monsoon: Mid-Feb to Mid-June)
- **Primary Crops**: Aus Rice, Jute, Maize, Early Vegetables.
- **Hazards**: Nor'westers (Kalbaishakhi), Heat Wave, Pre-monsoon Drought.
- **Critical Stage**: Jute sowing, Aus vegetative growth.

### 2. Kharif-II (Monsoon: Mid-June to Mid-Oct)
- **Primary Crops**: Aman Rice (Transplant & Broadcast), Jute, Aus Harvest.
- **Hazards**: Flash Flood, Riverine Flood, Tropical Cyclone, Heavy Rainfall.
- **Critical Stage**: Aman transplanting (July), Tillering (Aug), Flowering (Sept).

### 3. Rabi (Winter: Mid-Oct to Mid-Feb)
- **Primary Crops**: Boro Rice, Potato, Wheat, Pulses (Chickpea, Lentil), Oilseeds.
- **Hazards**: Cold Wave, Frost, Winter Drought, Salinity Intrusion (Coastal).
- **Critical Stage**: Boro seedling (Nov), Potato tuber formation (Dec-Jan).

documents.content:
# BRRI Stress-Tolerant Rice Varieties Database
## Used for Post-Hazard Replanting Recommendations

### Submergence Tolerant (Flood)
- **BRRI Dhan51**: Tolerates submergence up to 10-12 days. (Kharif-II)
- **BRRI Dhan52**: Tolerates submergence up to 2 weeks. (Kharif-II)
- **BRRI Dhan56**: Short duration (110 days), good for flash flood recovery.

### Drought Tolerant (Rainfed Aus/Upland)
- **BRRI Dhan57**: Deep rooting, drought-tolerant. (Aus)
- **BRRI Dhan61**: Tolerates moisture stress at reproductive stage.
- **BRRI Dhan71**: Upland rice, suitable for Barind tract.

### Salinity Tolerant (Coastal)
- **BRRI Dhan53**: Tolerates EC up to 8-10 dS/m. (Kharif-II)
- **BRRI Dhan54**: Highly salt-tolerant, suitable for Rabi season in coastal belts.
- **BRRI Dhan55**: Tolerant to tidal surge salinity.

### Cold Tolerant (Boro Seedling Stage)
- **BRRI Dhan36**: Tolerates low temperature at seedling stage.
- **BRRI Dhan62**: Cold tolerant for late Rabi planting.

documents.title: Post Disaster Disease Sops
documents.content:
# VETERINARY EMERGENCY PROTOCOLS (DLS)
## Triggered ONLY when HazardNet Severity >= 0.65 (High/Severe)

### 1. Anthrax & Black Quarter (Post-Flood)
- **Trigger:** Flooding followed by sudden cattle deaths with dark blood from natural orifices.
- **SOP:** DO NOT open carcasses (prevents spore formation). Bury deep (6 ft) with quicklime. Ring-vaccinate all healthy cattle within a 10km radius with Anthrax Spore Vaccine (Department of Livestock Services).

### 2. Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) & Hemorrhagic Septicemia (Post-Cold Wave/Transition)
- **Trigger:** Cold Wave or sudden temperature drops affecting immunocompromised livestock.
- **SOP:** Isolate infected animals immediately. Provide soft, easily digestible fodder and potassium permanganate mouth washes. Vaccinate with Polyvalent FMD vaccine.

### 3. Avian Influenza & Newcastle Disease (Post-Cyclone/Flood)
- **Trigger:** Poultry sheds damaged, wild migratory birds mixing with domestic flocks due to habitat loss.
- **SOP:** Cull infected flocks safely under DLS supervision (PPE required). Disinfect sheds with 2% sodium hypochlorite. Ban movement of live poultry from the 3km containment zone.

documents.title: Regional Vulnerability Profiles
documents.content:
# Regional Vulnerability & Hazard Profiles
## Context: Bangladesh Spatial Hazard Routing

### 1. Coastal & Tidal Zones (Khulna, Satkhira, Bagerhat, Patuakhali, Barguna, Bhola)
- **Primary Hazards:** Tropical Cyclone, Severe Local Storm, Salinity Intrusion, Tidal Surge.
- **Agro-Context:** Coastal saline soils, mangrove (Sundarbans) proximity, shrimp-rice rotation.
- **Specific LLM Instructions:** 
  - If `hazard == 'Tropical Cyclone'`, prioritize "sluice gate closure" and "salinity flushing".
  - If `hazard == 'Flood'`, treat as "Tidal Surge" (saltwater), NOT riverine freshwater. Recommend gypsum application and salt-tolerant varieties (BR-11).

### 2. Haor Basin & Wetlands (Sunamganj, Sylhet, Netrokona, Kishoreganj, Habiganj)
- **Primary Hazards:** Flash Flood (Pre-monsoon), Severe Local Storm (Kalbaishakhi).
- **Agro-Context:** Bowl-shaped depressions, Boro rice cultivation in winter, highly vulnerable to sudden pre-monsoon (March-April) flash floods from upstream hills.
- **Specific LLM Instructions:**
  - If `hazard == 'Flash Flood'` and season is `Kharif-I` (Mar-May), trigger "Emergency Early Harvest" protocol for Boro rice.
  - Do NOT recommend embankment reinforcement (ineffective in Haors); recommend rapid harvesting and elevated seed storage.

### 3. Barind Tract & Northern Drought Zones (Rajshahi, Rangpur, Nawabganj, Dinajpur, Thakurgaon)
- **Primary Hazards:** Drought, Heat Wave, Cold Wave.
- **Agro-Context:** Pleistocene elevated tract, red clay soil, high groundwater dependence, rainfed Aus and irrigated Boro.
- **Specific LLM Instructions:**
  - If `hazard == 'Drought'`, prioritize Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), mulching, and shifting to short-duration pulses (Masoor) if Boro fails.
  - If `hazard == 'Cold Wave'`, focus on Rabi crops (Potato, Wheat, Mustard) and recommend irrigation to mitigate frost.

### 4. Active Floodplains & River Basins (Jamuna, Padma, Meghna basins - e.g., Sirajganj, Jamalpur, Tangail, Comilla)
- **Primary Hazards:** Flood (Riverine), River Erosion.
- **Agro-Context:** Deep alluvial soils, high agricultural density, monsoon (Jul-Sep) inundation.
- **Specific LLM Instructions:**
  - If `hazard == 'Flood'`, treat as "Riverine Monsoon Flood". Focus on drainage, floating agriculture (Baira), and post-flood bacterial leaf blight management.

### 5. Hill & Elevated Regions (Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Rangamati, Bandarban, Khagrachari)
- **Primary Hazards:** Severe Local Storm, Flash Flood, Landslide (Note: Landslide not in HazardNet, but storm causes it).
- **Agro-Context:** Slope agriculture, Jhum cultivation, high rainfall.
- **Specific LLM Instructions:**
  - If `hazard == 'Severe Local Storm'`, prioritize hill-side crop protection and warning against working on steep slopes during Kalbaishakhi storms.

documents.title: Skill 01 Pipeline Interpretation
documents.content:
# SKILL 01: HazardNet Pipeline & Uncertainty Interpretation

## OBJECTIVE
Safely interpret HazardNet TFLite edge-inference outputs and map them to advisory urgency levels.

## HAZARDNET OUTPUT SCHEMA
The model outputs two values:
1. `hazard_class`: Categorical (Flood, Cyclone, Drought, etc.)
2. `severity_score`: Continuous float [0.0 to 1.0] representing physical impact magnitude.
3. `confidence_bin`: Categorical (Certain ≥0.85, Probable 0.70-0.85, Uncertain <0.70).

## ADVISORY ROUTING MATRIX (STRICT PROTOCOL)
You MUST map the model outputs to the following advisory tiers:

| Severity Score | Confidence Bin | Advisory Tier | Action Required |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **≥ 0.75** | **Certain** | 🔴 EMERGENCY | Immediate evacuation/harvest. Trigger DAE Emergency SOP. |
| **≥ 0.75** | **Probable** | 🟠 HIGH ALERT | Prepare resources. Pre-position relief. Monitor hourly. |
| **0.40 - 0.74** | **Certain/Probable** | 🟡 WATCH | Proactive mitigation (e.g., clear drains, apply fungicides). |
| **< 0.40** | **Any** | 🟢 ROUTINE | Standard seasonal awareness. No urgent action. |
| **Any** | **Uncertain** | ⚠️ CAUTIONARY | "Probabilistic Outlook". Emphasize local ground-truthing. |

## EDGE CASE HANDLING
- **Suspicious Zeros**: If `severity_score == 0.0` but `hazard_class != 'None'`, treat as "Data Gap / Sensor Occlusion" (e.g., heavy cloud cover on optical bands). Advise reliance on SAR/ERA5 climate data.
- **Conflicting Signals**: If Open-Meteo predicts heavy rain but HazardNet predicts Drought (due to lag in soil moisture response), prioritize the **HazardNet temporal context** but add a caveat about rapid-onset flash floods.

documents.title: Skill 02 Meteo Satellite Literacy
documents.content:
# SKILL 02: Meteorological & Satellite Data Literacy

## OBJECTIVE
Interpret the 15-channel HazardNet input tensor and Open-Meteo/NASA API forecasts to explain the "Why" behind the prediction to farmers.

## SATELLITE BAND INTERPRETATION
- **SAR (VV/VH)**: Represents surface water and vegetation structure. High VV/VH ratio changes indicate flooding or cyclone windthrow (lodging).
- **Optical (NIR/Red)**: NDVI drops indicate crop stress (drought/salinity). 
- **ERA5 Climate (Temp/Precip/Soil)**: Represents the atmospheric driver. 

## OPEN-METEO FORECAST LIMITATIONS (CRITICAL FOR ACCURACY)
- **7-Day Horizon**: Highly accurate deterministic forecast. Use for tactical advice (e.g., "Harvest in next 48h").
- **15-Day Horizon**: Probabilistic. Use for strategic advice (e.g., "Prepare drainage").
- **DO NOT** invent specific millimeter rainfall amounts for >7 day horizons. Use qualitative terms ("above-normal monsoon surge", "prolonged dry spell").

## DATA FUSION LOGIC
If SAR shows standing water (Flood) BUT Open-Meteo shows 0mm precipitation:
→ **Diagnosis**: Riverine flood or tidal surge (not local rainfall).
→ **Action**: Advise sluice gate management (Coastal) or embankment monitoring (Riverine), NOT local drainage.

documents.title: Skill 03 Bmd Early Warning
documents.content:
# SKILL 03: BMD Early Warning Signal Integration

## OBJECTIVE
Align HazardNet predictions with official Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) warning signals for public trust and legal compliance.

## CYCLONE WARNING SIGNALS
- **Signal 1 (Dangerous)**: HazardNet Severity > 0.4. Action: Monitor.
- **Signal 3 (Great Danger)**: HazardNet Severity > 0.7. Action: Evacuate to shelters.
- **Signal 7-10 (Extreme)**: HazardNet Severity > 0.9. Action: Absolute lockdown, secure livestock.

## HEAVY RAINFALL / FLASH FLOOD ALERTS
- **Yellow Alert**: 15-day forecast shows >100mm rain. HazardNet Severity > 0.5.
- **Red Alert**: 7-day forecast shows >200mm rain. HazardNet Severity > 0.8.
- **Protocol**: Always reference "In alignment with BMD Red/Yellow Alert protocols..." in the advisory header.

documents.title: Skill 04 Dae Agricultural Sop
documents.content:
# SKILL 04: DAE Agricultural Disaster SOPs

## OBJECTIVE
Provide crop-stage-specific interventions based on DAE guidelines.

## FLOOD / FLASH FLOOD SOP
- **Pre-Event (Severity > 0.6)**: Harvest mature crops immediately. Move seeds to elevated storage.
- **Post-Event (Water recedes < 5 days)**: Wash seedlings with clean water. Apply Urea (20 kg/ha) for recovery.
- **Post-Event (Water recedes > 10 days)**: Crop loss >80%. Switch to short-duration crops (e.g., BRRI Dhan56, Moong Dal).

## DROUGHT / HEAT WAVE SOP
- **Vegetative Stage**: Implement Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD). Apply mulch.
- **Reproductive Stage (Flowering)**: Spray water on canopy during 12 PM - 3 PM. Apply Potash (MOP) to improve cell turgor.
- **Severe (Severity > 0.8)**: Advise crop insurance claim initiation via local UP office.

## SALINITY INTRUSION SOP (Coastal: Satkhira, Khulna, Bagerhat)
- **Pre-Surge**: Close all polder sluice gates. 
- **Post-Surge**: Apply agricultural gypsum (2-3 tons/ha) to displace sodium. Flush with freshwater if available.

documents.title: Skill 05 Brri Variety Matching
documents.content:
# SKILL 05: BRRI Stress-Tolerant Variety Matching

## OBJECTIVE
Recommend specific BRRI rice varieties based on the predicted hazard and severity.

## VARIETY MATCHING MATRIX
| Hazard | Severity | Recommended BRRI Variety | Tolerance Trait |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Flood** | High | BRRI Dhan51, Dhan52 | Submergence (up to 14 days) |
| **Flood** | Moderate | BRRI Dhan56 | Short duration (escape strategy) |
| **Drought** | High | BRRI Dhan57, Dhan61 | Deep rooting, moisture stress |
| **Salinity** | High | BRRI Dhan53, Dhan54 | Tolerates EC up to 10 dS/m |
| **Cold Wave** | High | BRRI Dhan36, Dhan62 | Seedling stage cold tolerance |

## PROTOCOL
When advising post-disaster replanting, you MUST include the specific BRRI variety name and the local seed distributor (e.g., BADC or local NGO).

documents.title: Skill 06 International Frameworks
documents.content:
# SKILL 06: International Framework Alignment

## OBJECTIVE
Frame advisories within global standards for climate adaptation.

## FAO (Food and Agriculture Organization)
- Reference "FAO Guidelines for Climate-Smart Agriculture".
- Emphasize post-disaster soil health (e.g., green manuring after floods).

## WMO (World Meteorological Organization)
- Reference "WMO Seasonal Climate Outlooks" for 15-day to 3-month horizons.
- Use WMO standardized terminology (e.g., "Above Normal Precipitation", "Meteorological Drought").

## SENDAI FRAMEWORK FOR DISASTER RISK REDUCTION
- Align advisories with "Target G: Increase availability of and access to early warning systems".
- Frame the HazardNet advisory as an "Anticipatory Action" mechanism.

documents.title: 15 Band Tensor Logic
documents.content:
# SKILL: 15-Band Tensor Interpretation
## OBJECTIVE
Translate HazardNet's 15-channel input tensor anomalies into physical hazard drivers.

## BAND MAPPING & INTERPRETATION
1. **SAR_VV & SAR_VH (Sentinel-1):** 
   - *Logic:* VV is sensitive to surface water (double bounce / specular reflection) and wind roughness. VH is sensitive to volume scattering from vegetation.
   - *Action:* If VV drops sharply while VH drops → **Standing floodwater**. If VV spikes while VH drops → **Cyclone windthrow** (vegetation canopy destroyed, ground exposed).
2. **Blue, Red, NIR, SWIR (Sentinel-2/Landsat):**
   - *Logic:* NIR measures chlorophyll content and biomass health. SWIR measures plant tissue water content.
   - *Action:* NIR drop + SWIR spike → **Severe Drought / Moisture Stress**. NIR drop + Red spike → **Post-flood crop rotting or leaf chlorosis**.
3. **Temp_2m, Max_Temp, Min_Temp, Dewpoint (ERA5):**
   - *Logic:* Diurnal temperature range (Max - Min) and relative humidity proxy (Temp - Dewpoint).
   - *Action:* Min_Temp < 283.15K (10°C) for > 3 consecutive days → **Cold Wave** (Rabi crop/Boro seedling injury). High Dewpoint + High Temp_2m → **Extreme Heat Stress** (spike in crop transpiration loss and livestock heat stroke).
4. **Precip, Soil_W1, Soil_W3, Solar_Rad:**
   - *Logic:* Soil_W1 (0-7cm surface) responds immediately; Soil_W3 (0-1m root zone) reflects cumulative water availability.
   - *Action:* High Precip + Soil_W1 saturation → **Flash Flood Trigger**. Zero Precip + Soil_W3 drying below wilting point → **Root-Zone Agricultural Drought**.

documents.title: Climate Drivers
documents.content:
# SKILL: ERA5 Reanalysis Climate Drivers
## OBJECTIVE
Interpret atmospheric, surface temperature, precipitation, and soil layer ERA5 variables driving agricultural hazards in Bangladesh.

## DRIVER THRESHOLDS
- **Precipitation Anomaly:** Daily rainfall > 100mm/day in Meghalaya/Assam catchments triggers transboundary flash floods in Sylhet/Sunamganj within 24–48 hours.
- **Root Zone Soil Moisture (Soil_W3):** Volumetric water content < 0.15 m³/m³ in Barind Tract (Rajshahi, Dinajpur) signals deep agricultural drought.
- **Diurnal Thermal Extremes:** Max_Temp > 38°C (311.15K) accompanied by Solar_Rad > 22 MJ/m²/day causes heat blast / spikelet sterility in Boro rice at flowering stage.

documents.title: Optical Stress
documents.content:
# SKILL: Optical Multispectral Vegetation Stress Indices
## OBJECTIVE
Derive vegetation canopy health, soil moisture deficit, and flood debris signals from Blue, Red, NIR, and SWIR bands.

## SPECTRAL FORMULATIONS
- **NDVI = (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red):** Healthy crop > 0.6; Water < 0.0; Bare Soil 0.1–0.2.
- **NDWI = (Green/NIR - SWIR) / (Green/NIR + SWIR):** Water body and canopy liquid water content. NDWI > 0.3 indicates waterlogging.
- **NDMI = (NIR - SWIR) / (NIR + SWIR):** Crop canopy moisture stress. NDMI < 0.1 indicates severe water stress.

## ANOMALY INTERPRETATION
- **Rapid NDVI Collapse (> 40% drop in 5 days):** Crop inundation, cyclone lodging, or severe pest infestation.
- **SWIR Rise with Stable Red:** Canopy dehydration during prolonged dry spells or high evaporative demand.

documents.title: Sar Anomalies
documents.content:
# SKILL: SAR Anomalies (Sentinel-1 VV/VH)
## OBJECTIVE
Interpret Synthetic Aperture Radar backscatter signals for all-weather, day-and-night flood inundation and windthrow detection.

## PHYSICAL MECHANISMS
- **Specular Reflection (Smooth Water):** Smooth open water reflects radar pulses away from the antenna, resulting in dark pixels (VV < -18 dB).
- **Double-Bounce Scattering (Flooded Vegetation):** Water beneath crop stalks causes double reflection between water surface and vertical stems, producing bright VV signatures (+2 to +5 dB anomaly).
- **Volume Scattering Loss (Lodging/Windthrow):** Flattened rice stalks lose structural canopy geometry, reducing VH backscatter (-4 to -8 dB drop).

## OPERATIONAL TRIAGE
- **Flood Inundation:** VV < -16 dB AND VH < -22 dB across > 15% of grid cells.
- **Submerged Boro Paddy:** VV double-bounce spike followed by VV dark surface drop as water level rises above canopy.

documents.title: Severity Binning
documents.content:
# SKILL: Severity Index Binning & Action Tiers
## OBJECTIVE
Map HazardNet's continuous Sigmoid output (0.0 to 1.0) to Bangladesh Government Action Tiers.

## BINNING PROTOCOL
- **0.00 - 0.33 (LOW / WATCH):** 
  - *Tone:* Informational & routine observation.
  - *Action:* Continue regular satellite surveillance. Maintain routine DAE advice. No emergency resource allocation required.
- **0.34 - 0.66 (MODERATE / WARNING):** 
  - *Tone:* Preparatory & proactive mobilization.
  - *Action:* Mobilize DAE field extension officers (BS). Pre-position flood-tolerant BRRI seeds. Inspect embankment integrity and clean drainage canals.
- **0.67 - 1.00 (HIGH / EMERGENCY):** 
  - *Tone:* Urgent / Crisis Response.
  - *Action:* Trigger BMD Signal 3+. Activate District Disaster Management Committees (DDMC). Issue WHO water purification tablet advisories and UNICEF child WASH protocols.

documents.title: Uncertainty Routing
documents.content:
# SKILL: Uncertainty Routing & Low-Confidence Mitigation
## OBJECTIVE
Handle predictions where HazardNet confidence score < 0.70 (70%) by injecting probabilistic framing and institutional cross-verification warnings.

## PROTOCOL FOR CONFIDENCE < 0.70
1. **Probabilistic Framing Mandate:** Prepend advisories with explicit WMO seasonal outlook caveats: *"Prediction contains moderate model uncertainty (Confidence < 70%). Treat as probabilistic risk scenario."*
2. **Cross-Verification Advice:** Instruct local agricultural officers (UAO/SAAO) and farmers to cross-reference with official Union Parishad notices and local BMD synoptic weather bulletins.
3. **No Irreversible Actions:** Do not advise drastic, irreversible early harvest if confidence is low unless verified by ground observation.

documents.title: Cold Wave
documents.content:
# SKILL: Cold Wave & Low Temperature Shock Protocol
## OBJECTIVE
Protect winter crops, Boro rice seedbeds, and poultry/livestock from severe winter temperature drops (< 10°C).

## PROTECTIVE ACTIONS
- **Boro Seedbed Irrigation:** Keep Boro rice seedbeds flooded with 3-5 cm water during cold nights and drain during sunny days to prevent seedling yellowing and cold injury.
- **Polythene Covering:** Cover seedbeds with transparent polythene sheets from 5 PM to 9 AM.
- **Fungicide Spraying:** Apply Mancozeb/Sulphur fungicides to potato fields to prevent Late Blight outbreak triggered by high humidity and cold temperatures.

documents.title: Drought Heat Wave
documents.content:
# SKILL: Agricultural Drought & Heat Wave Protocol
## OBJECTIVE
Combat root-zone water deficits and heat-induced spikelet sterility during severe dry spells in Barind and high-land zones.

## AGRONOMIC ADVISORIES
- **Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD):** Implement AWD irrigation technique in Boro paddy fields to reduce water consumption by 30% without yield penalty.
- **Heat Blast Suppression:** Maintain 2-3 cm standing water in paddy fields during flowering/panicle initiation stage to buffer canopy temperatures against extreme heat (>36°C).
- **Mulching:** Apply straw or plastic mulching in maize, potato, and vegetable plots to conserve soil moisture (Soil_W3).
- **Drought-Tolerant Varieties:** Recommend *BRRI Dhan56*, *BRRI Dhan66*, and BARI Drought-Tolerant Wheat/Maize varieties.

documents.title: Flood Flash Flood
documents.content:
# SKILL: Flood & Flash Flood Response Protocol
## OBJECTIVE
Deliver actionable crop protection, embankment monitoring, and post-inundation recovery advisories for flood and flash flood events in Bangladesh.

## PRE-EVENT ACTIONS (Severity > 0.50)
- **Harvest Priority:** Harvest mature Boro/Aman paddy immediately if crops are at 80%+ maturity (dough to ripe stage) to avoid total inundation loss.
- **Seedbed Protection:** Raise seedbed perimeters with bamboo fencing and polythene covers; prepare floating seedbeds (*Baira*) in low-lying Haor basins.
- **Livestock Safety:** Move cattle and poultry to elevated embankments (*Killa*) or highland shelters.

## POST-FLOOD RECOVERY (Water Recession)
- **Soil Fertility:** Apply 20 kg/ha Urea and 10 kg/ha MOP once floodwaters recede to restore submerged root vitality.
- **Replanting / Floating Seedbed Varieties:**
  - *BRRI Dhan51 / BRRI Dhan52:* Submergence-tolerant rice varieties for up to 14–21 days of total inundation.
  - *BRRI Dhan56 / BRRI Dhan57:* Short-duration varieties for late-season escape cropping.

documents.title: Severe Local Storm
documents.content:
# SKILL: Severe Local Storm & Kalbaishakhi Protocol
## OBJECTIVE
Mitigate Nor'wester (Kalbaishakhi) squalls, lightning, and hail damage during pre-monsoon (March-May).

## SAFETY & CROP ADVISORIES
- **Lightning Avoidance:** Farmers must clear open paddy fields immediately upon hearing thunder; avoid shelter under isolated trees.
- **Hail Damage Management:** Drain standing hail meltwater quickly to prevent root rot; apply light nitrogen fertilizer to recover damaged vegetative tissues.
- **Fruit / Crop Netting:** Use protective shading/netting over high-value horticulture and fruit orchards (mango, lychee).

documents.title: Tropical Cyclone
documents.content:
# SKILL: Tropical Cyclone & Coastal Surge Protocol
## OBJECTIVE
Mitigate catastrophic windthrow, saline water intrusion, and coastal polder breaches during Bay of Bengal cyclones.

## COASTAL EMERGENCY PROTOCOLS
- **Polder & Sluice Gate Control:** Close all coastal polder sluice gates immediately to prevent marine saline water entry into freshwater agricultural zones.
- **Crop Lodging Mitigation:** Tie standing sugarcane, banana, and maize stalks in bundles (*Propping*) to withstand high-velocity gale force winds.
- **Post-Surge Salinity Remediation:** Apply Gypsum (2-3 tonnes/hectare) and organic compost post-surge to leach excess Sodium (Na+) ions from root zones.
- **Saline-Tolerant Cultivars:** Promote *BRRI Dhan53*, *BRRI Dhan54*, and *BRRI Dhan67* (tolerates up to 8-10 dS/m salinity).

documents.title: Barc Climate Signatures
documents.content:
# SKILL: BARC Agro-Climatic Baselines (Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council)
## OBJECTIVE
Cross-reference Agro-Ecological Zones (AEZ 1 to 30) for baseline soil texture, land type (F0 to F4), and seasonal risk signatures.

## AEZ CLASSIFICATION HIGHLIGHTS
- **AEZ 1 (Old Himalayan Piedmont Plain):** Sandy loam soils, high vulnerability to cold waves and drought.
- **AEZ 2 (Active Tista Floodplain - Kurigram, Gaibandha):** Medium High to Medium Low land; extreme riverbank erosion and flash floods.
- **AEZ 13 (Sylhet Basin / Haor):** Very low land (F3/F4); 100% early flash flood threat during April-May Boro harvest.
- **AEZ 18 (Young Meghna Estuarine Floodplain):** Salinity intrusion and cyclone surge risk.

documents.title: Bari Crop Protocols
documents.content:
# SKILL: BARI Crop Protocols (Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute)
## OBJECTIVE
Provide non-rice crop advisories (Maize, Potato, Wheat, Pulses, Oilseeds) under climate stress.

## POTATO & VEGETABLES
- **Late Blight Alert:** When relative humidity > 85% and temperature between 12-20°C, spray Mancozeb (2g/L) preventively.
- **Flood Drainage:** Construct 30 cm deep drainage trenches around potato/vegetable beds to prevent root asphyxiation.

## MAIZE & PULSES
- **Waterlogging:** Maize is highly sensitive to root-zone saturation; drain field within 12 hours.
- **BARI Varieties:** *BARI Gom-33* (heat/blast tolerant wheat), *BARI Chhola-9* (drought tolerant chickpea).

documents.title: Brri Rice Protocols
documents.content:
# SKILL: BRRI Rice Protocols (Bangladesh Rice Research Institute)
## OBJECTIVE
Provide exact seed variety and agronomic recommendations based on hazard type.

## FLOOD / FLASH FLOOD (Submergence)
- **Pre-Event (Severity > 0.5):** Harvest mature Aman/Boro rice immediately if at dough/ripe stage.
- **Post-Event (Water recedes < 7 days):** Apply Urea (20 kg/ha) once water recedes to encourage tiller revival.
- **Replanting Varieties:** 
  - *BRRI Dhan51* (Tolerates 10-14 days complete submergence via SUB1 gene).
  - *BRRI Dhan52* (Tolerates 14-21 days submergence; high yielding).
  - *BRRI Dhan56* (Short duration, 110 days, drought-escape strategy).

## SALINITY INTRUSION (Coastal: Khulna, Satkhira, Bagerhat)
- **Pre-Event:** Close all polder sluice gates.
- **Post-Event:** Apply Gypsum (2-3 t/ha) to displace Na+ ions.
- **Replanting Varieties:**
  - *BRRI Dhan53* (Tolerates EC up to 8-10 dS/m).
  - *BRRI Dhan54* (Highly salt-tolerant for Rabi season).
  - *BRRI Dhan67* (Salt-tolerant at seedling and reproductive stages).

documents.title: Dae Extension Sop
documents.content:
# SKILL: DAE Extension Standard Operating Procedure (Department of Agricultural Extension)
## OBJECTIVE
Guide Sub-Assistant Agriculture Officers (SAAO) and Upazila Agriculture Officers (UAO) in field triage, damage reporting, and emergency input distribution.

## SAAO FIELD ACTION STEPS
1. **Block Triage:** Conduct physical inspection within 24 hours of hazard occurrence across all designated agricultural blocks.
2. **Loss Assessment:** Report damaged area (hectares), affected farmers, and crop stage via DAE Krishok App / Form-A to UAO.
3. **Input Distribution:** Coordinate emergency distribution of BRRI/BARI seeds, fertilizer kits, and mechanical harvesters (Combine Harvesters).

documents.title: Bmd Warning Signals
documents.content:
# SKILL: BMD Warning Signal Mapping (Bangladesh Meteorological Department)
## OBJECTIVE
Align HazardNet predictions with official Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) signals for public trust and institutional compliance.

## CYCLONE WARNING SIGNALS
- **Distant Cautionary Signal 1:** HazardNet Severity 0.25 - 0.40. *Action:* Keep tracking storm track in Bay of Bengal.
- **Local Warning Signal 3:** HazardNet Severity 0.41 - 0.65. *Action:* Ports warned, fishing boats return to shore, farmers prepare for wind gusts.
- **Danger Signal 5 - 7:** HazardNet Severity 0.66 - 0.80. *Action:* Evacuate coastal lowlands to cyclone shelters; secure livestock.
- **Great Danger Signal 8 - 10:** HazardNet Severity > 0.80. *Action:* Extreme crisis; total lockdown; full disaster response.

## HEAVY RAINFALL / FLASH FLOOD ALERTS
- **Yellow Alert:** Rainfall 44 - 88 mm/24hr. Clearing drainage channels.
- **Red Alert:** Rainfall > 88 mm/24hr. Immediate harvest and highland relocation.

documents.title: Wmo Seasonal Outlook
documents.content:
# SKILL: WMO Seasonal Outlook & ENSO/IOD Dynamics
## OBJECTIVE
Incorporate World Meteorological Organization (WMO) regional climate frameworks, ENSO (El Niño / La Niña), and Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) signatures into long-range agricultural risk advisories.

## CLIMATE DRIVER EFFECTS ON BANGLADESH
- **La Niña (+ Positive IOD):** Above-normal monsoon rainfall, higher frequency of severe river floods and pre-monsoon flash floods in Haor basin.
- **El Niño (- Negative IOD):** Below-normal rainfall, high probability of post-monsoon drought in Barind tract and high summer heat waves.

## OBJECTIVE
Implement Cash-for-Work, shock-responsive social protection, and early action intervention triggers.

documents.title: Who Post Disaster Health
documents.content:
# SKILL: WHO Post-Disaster Health Protocols
## OBJECTIVE
Trigger health advisories when HazardNet Severity > 0.65 (High Impact).

## FLOOD / CYCLONE HEALTH RISKS
1. **Waterborne Diseases (Cholera, Typhoid, Diarrhea):**
   - *Advisory:* "Boil all drinking water or use WHO-approved Aquatabs (1 tablet per 20L, wait 30 mins)."
   - *Action:* UNICEF/DPHE to deploy emergency tube-well testing for fecal contamination.
2. **Vector-Borne (Dengue, Malaria):**
   - *Advisory:* Stagnant water post-flood breeds Aedes mosquitoes. Use long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) and clear standing puddles near homesteads.
3. **Skin & Eye Infections:**
   - *Advisory:* Avoid wading in stagnant floodwater without rubber boots. Wash with soap and clean tube-well water immediately if exposed.

## COLD WAVE HEALTH RISKS
- *Advisory:* Vulnerable populations (children <5, elderly) must stay indoors. Keep warm clothing dry. Monitor closely for acute respiratory infection (ARI) or pneumonia symptoms.

documents.title: Aman Rice Stages
documents.content:
# SKILL: Aman Rice Agronomic Phenology & Hazard Vulnerability
## OBJECTIVE
Map monsoon-season Aman rice phenological stages to seasonal climate threats (Monsoon floods, late-season drought, coastal salinity).

## PHENOLOGICAL STAGES & THREATS
- **Seedbed (June - July):** Submergence risk from early monsoon rain. *Mitigation:* Floating seedbeds (*Baira*).
- **Transplanting (July - August):** High flood risk. *Mitigation:* Use 30-35 day old seedlings of *BRRI Dhan51/52*.
- **Vegetative / Tillering (August - September):** Submergence & stem borer attack. *Mitigation:* Apply balanced N-P-K fertilizer.
- **Flowering / Panicle Initiation (September - October):** Moisture stress / early drought (*Kharif-II drought*). *Mitigation:* Supplementary irrigation from local water bodies.
- **Harvest (November - December):** Cyclonic rain / lodging. *Mitigation:* Harvest at 80% grain yellowing.

documents.title: Boro Rice Stages
documents.content:
# SKILL: Boro Rice Agronomic Phenology & Hazard Vulnerability
## OBJECTIVE
Map winter/spring irrigated Boro rice phenological stages to cold waves, pre-monsoon flash floods, and heat waves.

## PHENOLOGICAL STAGES & THREATS
- **Seedbed (November - December):** Cold wave injury (< 10°C). *Mitigation:* Water inundation at night, polythene covering.
- **Transplanting (December - January):** Cold shock. *Mitigation:* Avoid transplanting during peak cold wave.
- **Vegetative / Booting (February - March):** Water stress. *Mitigation:* Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD).
- **Flowering / Panicle (March - April):** Heat wave (>35°C) & Kalbaishakhi hail storms. *Mitigation:* Maintain standing water layer.
- **Harvest (April - May):** Haor flash floods in Sylhet/Sunamganj/Kurigram. *Mitigation:* Harvest at 80% ripeness using combine harvesters.

documents.title: Rabi Vegetables
documents.content:
# SKILL: Rabi Crops & Winter Vegetables Phenology
## OBJECTIVE
Map winter non-rice crops (Potato, Mustard, Wheat, Tomato, Pulses) to cold wave, late blight, and unseasonal rainfall hazards.

## AGRONOMIC GUIDELINES
- **Potato (Nov - Feb):** Late Blight fungal attack during fog/cold wave. Spray preventive copper oxychloride or Mancozeb.
- **Mustard (Oct - Jan):** Aphid infestation during warm winter snaps. Apply bio-pesticides or neem oil.
- **Wheat (Nov - Mar):** Wheat Blast disease during humid warm spell. Use *BARI Gom-33*.
